fields.front: A scientific approach that applies principles of behavior to improve socially significant outcomes and uses experimentation to identify functional relations.
Anything an organism does that can be observed and measured.
A single instance of behavior; an action of the effector system.
Any event or condition that affects an organism through its receptors.
A process in which a behavior increases in future frequency due to its consequences.
Presenting a stimulus after a response that increases future responding.
Removing or reducing a stimulus after a response that increases future responding.
A process in which a behavior decreases in future frequency due to its consequences.
Presenting a stimulus after a response that decreases future responding.
Removing a stimulus after a response that decreases future responding.
Withholding reinforcement for a previously reinforced response, leading to a decrease in its frequency.
A stimulus that signals the availability of reinforcement for a particular response.
An environmental event that momentarily alters the value of a reinforcer and the frequency of behavior that has produced that reinforcer.
An MO that increases the effectiveness of a reinforcer and evokes behavior that has produced that reinforcer.
An MO that decreases the effectiveness of a reinforcer and abates behavior that has produced that reinforcer.
A systematic process for identifying the function of problem behavior and variables maintaining it.
Data collection of Antecedents, Behavior, and Consequences to identify functional relations.
An event or condition that occurs immediately before a behavior.
An event or condition that follows a behavior and affects its future frequency.
A document detailing strategies to reduce problem behavior and teach replacement skills based on FBA results.
Reinforcing one set of responses while withholding reinforcement for others.
Differential Reinforcement of Alternative behavior: reinforce a functional alternative to the problem behavior.
Differential Reinforcement of Incompatible behavior: reinforce a behavior that cannot occur simultaneously with the problem behavior.
Differential Reinforcement of Other behavior: reinforce the absence of the problem behavior for a specified interval.
Differential Reinforcement of Low rates: reinforce when the behavior occurs at or below a criterion rate.
Differential Reinforcement of High rates: reinforce when the behavior occurs at or above a criterion rate.
An added stimulus or cue that increases the likelihood of a correct response.
Systematically reducing prompts to transfer stimulus control to the natural SD.
Differentially reinforcing successive approximations toward a target behavior.
Teaching a complex skill by linking discrete responses in a specific sequence.
Breaking a complex skill into smaller, teachable steps.
The occurrence of a learned behavior under different, untrained conditions (people, settings, stimuli).
Sustained performance of a learned behavior over time after instruction ends.
Establishing oneself or a stimulus as a conditioned reinforcer by associating with existing reinforcers.
Procedures to identify potential reinforcers based on choice and engagement.
Teaching an appropriate communicative response that serves the same function as problem behavior.
Elapsed time from the onset of a stimulus to the initiation of a response.
Elapsed time between two consecutive responses.
Frequency of responses per unit of time.
Count of response occurrences.
Total time a behavior occurs from onset to offset.
The physical form or shape of a behavior; what it looks like.
The intensity or force of a response.
Reinforcement delivered after every occurrence of the target response.
Reinforcement delivered on some, but not all, occurrences of the response.
A schedule in which reinforcement is delivered after a fixed number of responses (e.g., FR5).
A schedule in which reinforcement is delivered after a variable number of responses around an average (e.g., VR5).
A schedule in which the first response after a fixed time interval is reinforced (e.g., FI 2 min).
A schedule in which the first response after variable time intervals is reinforced around an average (e.g., VI 2 min).
The extent to which goals, procedures, and outcomes are acceptable, important, and meaningful to stakeholders.
